The challenge

What makes construction & contracting different.

01

RFQs arrive as emails with PDF BOQs and drawings, estimators retype line items, and clarification deadlines are tracked in personal inboxes.

02

Progress, manpower and material use come from WhatsApp groups and paper registers, so the project manager sees the true position days late.

03

Material requests go by phone and are approved without a check against BOQ balance or site stock, so sites over-order or stop work for a missing item.

04

Near misses go unreported, serious incidents are relayed by phone with details lost, and statutory notices and registers depend on one person's memory.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for construction & contracting.

01

Bid desk

RFQ register, BOQ extraction mapped to your rate library, vendor quote requests and deadline reminders, with the estimator approving every rate.

02

One daily site report

Progress against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and hindrances in one mobile form that works offline and syncs later.

03

Labor attendance reconciliation

Headcount from biometric or app-based attendance matched against reported manpower, so subcontractor bills can be checked against who was actually on site.

04

Material requests with approvals

Requests checked against BOQ balance, drawing revision and site stock, routed by value, ordered by purchase and received with challan photos.

05

Safety incident and near-miss log

QR and WhatsApp reporting in the languages used on site, immediate phone escalation for serious events, investigations, corrective actions and draft statutory notices.

06

Snag rectification for clients

Snags from the developer's or tenant's handover assigned to your trades with due dates, closed with after photos and verified by the client's quality engineer.

Discover and enquireStandard4–6 weeks

RFQ and BOQ intake with extraction, vendor quotes and bid tracking

Tender and RFQ emails become entries in a bid register. AI extracts BOQ line items from spreadsheets and PDFs into a structured sheet mapped to your rate library and flags missing specifications, and the team tracks quotes, clarifications and deadlines until the estimator signs off.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Estimators spend days retyping BOQs from PDFs and spreadsheets, vendor quotes come back late or not at all, and pre-bid and clarification deadlines are tracked in personal inboxes. Good tenders are missed and rushed bids carry pricing errors.

Trigger

An RFQ, tender notice or addendum arrives in the bids mailbox or is downloaded from a client or government e-procurement portal, with drawings, specifications and a BOQ.

How it runs

  • Create a bid record with client, scope, pre-bid and submission dates, earnest money and document list, and post a summary to the bid channel for a go or no-go decision.
  • Extract BOQ items, units and quantities from spreadsheets or PDFs into a structured sheet, keeping the original item numbers and page references.
  • Suggest matching codes from the contractor's rate library, and flag items with no match, unclear specifications or unusual quantities for the estimator.
  • Send quote requests for unmatched materials and subcontract packages to approved vendors, and chase replies before the internal cut-off.
  • Track pre-bid queries, client clarifications and addenda against the affected BOQ items, and remind owners of every deadline.
  • Record submission, opening results, published competitor rates and the win or loss reason for use in future bids.

Human checkpoint

The chief estimator reviews every extracted line against the source document and approves every rate; extraction stays a draft until checked. A director approves the go or no-go decision, the margin and the final submission.

Tools

ACAnthropic ClaudePPythonAAirtablenn8nSSlackMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • Bids mailbox and document storage
  • Government e-procurement portals such as CPPP and state portals
  • Rate library and estimation spreadsheets
  • ERP such as SAP or Tally for the vendor master

Data & consent

Works on tender documents, drawings and vendor quotes, which are commercially confidential: they stay in the contractor's own workspace with access limited to the bid team. Client documents are used only for the bid in question, and model calls run under terms that exclude training on the data. Vendor contacts come from the approved vendor master.

What we deliver

  • Bid register with deadlines and owners
  • BOQ extraction workflow with a review screen
  • Rate library mapping rules
  • Vendor quote requests and tracking
  • Bid pipeline and win-loss report

How we measure it

  • Bids submitted before deadline
  • Estimator hours per bid
  • BOQ extraction accuracy after review
  • Vendor quote response rate
  • Win rate by client and work type

Build and payAdvanced5–8 weeks

Daily site reports, labor attendance and material approvals

Site engineers file one mobile daily report covering work done against plan, photos, manpower by subcontractor, equipment, materials received and material requests. Attendance is reconciled, requests are checked against BOQ balance and routed by value, and managers get a daily digest.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Progress, labor counts and material needs arrive as WhatsApp photos, calls and paper registers. Project managers see slippage days late, subcontractor bills cannot be checked against actual manpower, and materials are ordered without checking BOQ balance or site stock.

Trigger

The site engineer opens the daily report before the end of the shift, or raises a material request between reports.

How it runs

  • Collect activities and quantities against the planned schedule, location-tagged photos, manpower by trade and subcontractor, equipment hours, materials received with challan photos, and hindrances, in a mobile form that also works offline.
  • Pull headcount from biometric or app-based attendance where the system exposes an API or export, and flag gaps against the manpower reported for each subcontractor.
  • Check each material request against the BOQ balance, the current drawing revision and site stock, and flag requests above balance for the quantity surveyor.
  • Route requests for approval by value, from site in-charge to project manager to purchase head, with purchase raising the order in the ERP.
  • Compare reported progress with the schedule baseline, and send the project manager a daily digest of slippage, idle labor, stock risks and open issues.
  • Compile a weekly progress report with photos for the client or developer, reviewed by the project manager before it is shared.

Human checkpoint

The project manager reviews the daily digest and approves material requests within their limit; the purchase head approves higher values and the quantity surveyor approves anything above BOQ balance. Subcontractor bills are certified by the project manager and accounts, not by the automation.

Tools

NNext.jsSSupabasenn8nWBWhatsApp Business PlatformACAnthropic ClaudeMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • Schedule in Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project
  • Site apps such as Powerplay or Procore
  • Biometric or app-based attendance
  • ERP such as SAP or Tally for purchase orders and stock
  • BOQ and drawing registers

Data & consent

Worker data is limited to name, ID, trade, subcontractor and attendance times; biometric templates stay in the attendance device or vendor system and are never copied. Photos show work, not faces, wherever possible. Attendance and wage-related records are kept for the periods labor rules require, with access limited to site administration and HR.

What we deliver

  • Offline-capable daily report form
  • Attendance reconciliation by subcontractor
  • Material request approval matrix with BOQ checks
  • Daily digest and weekly client report
  • Site dashboard by project

How we measure it

  • Daily reports submitted on time
  • Manpower variance between attendance and reports
  • Material request approval time
  • Requests above BOQ balance
  • Schedule variance by activity

Build and payStandard3–5 weeks

Safety incident and near-miss logging with immediate escalation

Anyone on site can report an injury, dangerous occurrence or near miss by WhatsApp or QR code, with photos. Serious events trigger immediate calls to the safety officer and project head, corrective actions are tracked, and statutory notices are drafted for the responsible person to file.

Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Near misses go unreported, serious incidents are relayed by phone with details lost, and the statutory notices and registers that labor law requires depend on one person remembering the deadlines. Corrective actions from one site rarely reach the next.

Trigger

A worker, supervisor or engineer scans the site safety QR code or messages the site safety number, or a toolbox talk or inspection records an unsafe condition.

How it runs

  • Capture what happened, where, who was involved, any injuries, photos and immediate actions in a short form offered in the languages used on site.
  • Classify severity using the safety officer's rules; fatal accidents, serious injuries and dangerous occurrences such as a scaffold or structure collapse trigger immediate calls and messages to the safety officer, site in-charge and project head.
  • Open an investigation record with timeline, witnesses, root-cause fields and corrective actions with owners and due dates.
  • Draft statutory notices and register entries from the record for the safety officer to complete and file within the deadlines the applicable rules set.
  • Track corrective actions to closure with photo evidence, and share lessons across sites in a weekly safety bulletin.
  • Report incidents, near misses, open actions and toolbox talk coverage by site and subcontractor.

Human checkpoint

The site safety officer owns every report and decides severity, investigation and closure; first aid, medical care and emergency response never wait for the automation. The safety officer or employer files statutory notices, and the system only drafts and reminds. The project head reviews serious incidents that day.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • State labor department portal for notices
  • Subcontractor master

  • Cloud telephony for escalation calls

Data & consent

Holds the worker's name, ID, injury description and photos, which are sensitive: access is limited to the safety officer, site head and HR, and photos record conditions rather than faces. Records are kept for the period the applicable labor rules and the contractor's insurer require, and reporters can stay anonymous for near misses.

What we deliver

  • Multilingual incident and near-miss reporting flow
  • Severity rules and escalation call tree
  • Investigation and corrective action tracker
  • Draft notice and register templates
  • Safety dashboard by site

How we measure it

  • Time from report to safety officer acknowledgement
  • Near misses reported by site
  • Corrective actions closed by due date
  • Statutory notices filed within deadline

Possession and move-inStandard4–6 weeks

Possession, fit-out handover and snag-list management

After the occupancy certificate or fit-out completion, buyers and tenants book handover slots, receive a final dues statement, report snags room by room with photos and track each item as the contractor fixes it and a quality engineer verifies it. Later defect reports follow the same path.

Residential developers · Commercial leasing & co-working · Construction & contracting

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Possession arrives in a rush: buyers call for dates and final dues, snag lists are written on paper during the walkthrough, and contractors receive them days later on WhatsApp. Items are closed without proof and reopened by unhappy buyers, and defect complaints after handover get lost although the developer remains responsible for years.

Trigger

The occupancy certificate is received and possession is offered for a tower, or a commercial floor's warm-shell or fit-out handover is ready; later, an owner or tenant reports a defect.

How it runs

  • Send the possession or handover offer with the final dues statement and document checklist, and offer handover slots by tower and floor.
  • During the pre-handover inspection, buyers or tenants log snags room by room with photos and a category, on a tablet with the handover executive or on their own phone.
  • Assign each snag to the responsible contractor or trade with a due date, and notify the contractor's site engineer.
  • Contractors close items with after photos, and the quality engineer verifies each closure before the buyer or tenant is asked to confirm.
  • Release keys or access once dues, documents and the agreed snags are complete, and record the handover acknowledgement.
  • Keep a defect reporting route open after handover, tracked as defect-liability tickets with the same assignment and verification steps.

Human checkpoint

The quality engineer verifies every closure and the CRM handover manager signs off each possession. Disputed snags, compensation questions and any structural concern go to the project head and, where needed, the structural consultant.

Tools

NNext.jsSSupabaseWBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8nRRetoolMPMicrosoft Power BI

Systems it connects

  • ERP for final dues and possession status
  • Real estate CRM or lease system
  • Contractor and vendor master
  • Facility helpdesk for post-handover defects

Data & consent

Uses unit, owner or tenant contact, dues status and snag photos of the property only. Contractors see the unit, location and snag, never buyer contact details. Handover and defect records are kept for at least the defect liability period, which RERA sets at five years from possession for units sold in registered projects.

What we deliver

  • Possession offer, dues and slot booking flow
  • Snag capture app with photo evidence
  • Contractor assignment and verification workflow
  • Defect-liability ticketing
  • Handover and snag dashboard

How we measure it

  • Offer-to-handover time
  • Snags closed by due date
  • Snag reopen rate
  • Defect tickets open beyond target
  • Handover satisfaction score
